resources.note: opencode has no per-agent channel for information that carries no authority: resources arrive as message content, and opencode references are project-wide directories or Git repositories.

model.name.note: A provider/model reference, for example in the agent's model field.

model.effort.note: Maps to the model variant (provider/model#variant). Variants come from the model's reasoning levels and from configuration, so the set is open; the host checks the variant at launch.

skills.note: Skills are discovered from configured paths; the skill permission action, keyed by skill name, limits which ones an agent may load.

mcpServers.note: Servers are configured under mcp.servers; permission rules on server_tool actions remove other servers' tools from the agent.

plan.note: Maps to the todowrite tool, enabled by experimental.todo true; the todos reach the host as tool metadata. The flag is experimental.

planFirst.auto.note: The built-in plan agent denies file edits outside its plan directory but not shell or MCP actions, and it has no plan-exit tool: the host must switch the session to the working agent once the plan is presented.

planFirst.ask.note: The plan agent's lock covers file edits only, so it cannot be enforced like a permission, and opencode has no plan approval step.

instance.new.note: Each work runs in a new session.

delivery.steer.note: Session prompts accept delivery steer, which joins the running work at the next step boundary.

reviewer.person.note: An ask rule prompts the user in the TUI, or emits a permission request that the host answers through the server API. A reject without a message ends the run, so the host rejects with a message for the agent to continue; it never replies always, which saves a project-wide allow rule that overrides ask rules.

reviewer.model.note: --auto approves every request that is not denied, without judging it; a reviewing model is only available through a third-party plugin.

directories.note: Maps to external_directory allow rules for the directory, with edit rules for writable ones.

read.note: The read action, matched on the file path; paths outside the project also pass the external_directory action. Shell commands are matched as shell actions, not as reads. Reads outside the zone are denied with external_directory deny rules. grep is matched on its pattern, not on paths, and returns line previews: when read has path rules, grep and glob are denied. Paths inside the project's git worktree count as inside and do not pass external_directory.

write.note: The edit action covers the edit, write and patch tools, matched on the file path; paths outside the project also pass the external_directory action. Shell commands are matched as shell actions, not as writes.

shell.note: The shell action, matched on each parsed command; directories the command reaches outside the project also pass the external_directory action. No operating-system sandbox.

network.note: The webfetch action, matched on the URL, and the websearch action. Network access by shell commands and MCP servers is not restricted. Redirect hops are checked only against deny rules, so an ask rule can be bypassed.

mcp.note: Each MCP tool is a permission action named server_tool, with characters other than letters, digits, _ and - replaced by underscores. Resources use the actions opencode_list_mcp_resources, matched on the server, and opencode_read_mcp_resource, matched on server:uri.

delegate.note: The subagent action, matched on the sub-agent name. A sub-agent runs with its own agent's permissions, not the parent's: the exporter must configure sub-agents no wider than the agent.

steps.description: Maximum number of model steps per run (agent steps). After it, tools are disabled until the next input. A positive integer.
